nodes.description: Address state variable storing the developer account set in the constructor and used by the is_developer authorization check.
Constructor of the BingoLight contract; assigns msg.sender to the developer state variable.
Constant function that derives three lottery numbers pseudo-randomly from block.blockhash of a caller supplied target block.
Privileged function gated by the is_developer modifier that calls suicide(msg.sender) and destroys the contract.
Modifier that reverts unless msg.sender equals the developer state variable; controls access to del().
Caller-supplied address used for developer assignment, access control comparison and as the suicide beneficiary.
Irreversible SELFDESTRUCT operation executed inside del(), sending the contract balance to msg.sender.
Use of block.blockhash(targetBlock) as a pseudo-randomness source in generateLuckyNumbers; miner-influenced and predictable.
uint256 parameter of generateLuckyNumbers selecting which historical block hash feeds the randomness computation.
Return parameter uint256[3] holding the generated lucky numbers.
bytes32 local variable holding block.blockhash results reused across loop iterations.
uint256 local variable holding each candidate random number in the range 1..10.
uint256 local constant set to 3, the number of lucky numbers required.
uint8 counter tracking how many unique lucky numbers have been accepted.
uint256 loop counter walking backwards through up to 255 prior blocks.
uint256 inner loop counter used to shift the block hash by 256**n.
uint8 index used to test whether a candidate number is already in lotteryLuckyNumbers.

edges.reason: The BingoLight constructor writes the developer state variable during deployment.
msg.sender is copied into the developer state variable in the constructor.
The is_developer modifier compares the untrusted msg.sender against the stored developer to authorize privileged calls.
The is_developer modifier reads the developer state variable as the trusted authority reference.
The is_developer modifier guards entry into del(), reverting for non-developer callers.
suicide(msg.sender) forwards the entire contract balance to the caller-supplied address.
del() unconditionally executes the suicide self-destruct operation.
The targetBlock parameter is consumed by generateLuckyNumbers to select the source block.
The caller-controlled targetBlock indexes block.blockhash, letting the caller influence the randomness input.
generateLuckyNumbers relies on block.blockhash as its only randomness source, which is predictable and miner-influenced.
The result of block.blockhash is stored in the blockHash local variable and reused for all generated numbers.
generateLuckyNumbers computes and stores candidate values in the newRnd local variable.
The currentN counter drives the while/for loop termination logic in generateLuckyNumbers.
The blockNumber counter drives the outer while loop that scans up to 255 prior blocks in generateLuckyNumbers.
The i index drives the inner for loop that checks for duplicate lucky numbers.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter is only used inside generateLuckyNumbers to pick the block whose hash seeds the randomness.
Return array parameter is written exclusively within generateLuckyNumbers and has no independent behaviour.
Local variable exists solely to hold block.blockhash results and is fully represented by the randomness unsafe operation.
Scratch variable for candidate random numbers local to the generateLuckyNumbers computation.
Local constant fixed at 3 controlling the number of lucky numbers generated.
Loop control counter confined to the generateLuckyNumbers unique-number selection logic.
Outer loop counter bounded at 255, meaningful only inside generateLuckyNumbers.
Inner loop counter used for byte shifting of the block hash inside generateLuckyNumbers.
Duplicate-check index local to the inner for loop of generateLuckyNumbers.
